name: 31438-multiimage-qwen36moe35bfp8-tp2
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3, ONE node, no router and no external cache tier.
parallelism: TP=2, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=16, warmup the first 10% and cooldown the last 10% (both mode=requests), bounded at 800 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm, ONE turn: four distinct images -- 512x512, 640x640, 768x768 and 768x1024 -- plus 32 text tokens in, ONE token out, ignore_eos, temperature 0.0, seed 42; ~2000 vision tokens per request. Five data sources rather than one because guidellm reads `images_per_request: N` as N TURNS. At ONE output token guidellm stamps no first-token boundary, so `time_to_first_token_ms` is None on every record and the ITL columns are empty by construction; `TPOT_MS` (`time_per_output_token_ms`) includes the first token and is the first-token read here.
purpose: A visual question-answering assistant reading four images per question for 16 concurrent users on two GPUs.
launch:
# sglang server arguments. Flat `key: value` only -- a nested block is dropped on read, and a
# dropped key means the engine runs without something this file declares.

model-path: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8
tp-size: 2

# Every image in the workload is byte-distinct (`content: gradient` varies by row as well as by
# seed), so a radix cache can only match the short chat preamble; leaving it on buys nothing
# measurable and adds run-to-run variance. The same property keeps the embedding cache -- keyed by
# multimodal item hash -- from ever returning a cross-request hit, so each request encodes its own
# four images. Keep that property if the workload is edited.
disable-radix-cache: true

random-seed: 42

# This model is hybrid linear/full attention. Read `max_mamba_cache_size` off the startup log and
# confirm it exceeds the sixteen concurrent streams, or the run is gated on admission rather than
# serving the declared load.
